dataset: Musashi Book V — Sky production provenance

evidence_policy.narrative_authority: All 26 local files under data/source/book5, read in full before web validation
evidence_policy.presence_rule: physically_present means on-page presence; letters, memories, reports, plans, distant names and possessions are mentioned_only
evidence_policy.coordinate_rule: No coordinates are emitted. Named real-world correspondence does not establish a narrative point.
evidence_policy.web_scope: Geography and historicity only after local corpus freeze; web sources cannot add narrative facts.

chapters.title: The Abduction
chapters.end_summary: Matahachi is moving with captive Otsū; Jōtarō is injured beside the road; Musashi is running back without yet knowing what happened.

chapters.title: The Warrior of Kiso
chapters.end_summary: Musashi and Gonnosuke are cooperating near Nobu Pond; Otsū remains missing and Jōtarō is reported heading toward Narai.

chapters.title: Poisonous Fangs
chapters.end_summary: Otsū remains under Matahachi's control on a back road toward Edo; the exact next stop is not established.

chapters.title: A Maternal Warning
chapters.end_summary: Musashi heads toward Kamisuwa without a confirmed lead; Gonnosuke and his mother remain together after the rematch.

chapters.title: A One-Night Love Affair
chapters.end_summary: Musashi remains at Shimosuwa overnight; no service commitment is made.

chapters.title: A Gift of Money
chapters.end_summary: Musashi is alive at the ravine under attack; Geki is already on the Wada route; Jōtarō's lead remains only reported.

chapters.title: A Cleansing Fire
chapters.end_summary: Musashi has escaped Buna Valley; Okō is tied near the burning cabin with Tōji and his band still in the area.

chapters.title: Playing with Fire
chapters.end_summary: Akemi is recovered disheveled near the inn; Jōtarō returns after being knocked out; the scarred rōnin is unidentified.

chapters.title: A Cricket in the Grass
chapters.end_summary: Jōtarō travels toward Edo under Daizō's coercive protection; Sukeichi accompanies them; Akemi is ahead with Jinnai's troupe.

chapters.title: The Pioneers
chapters.end_summary: Osugi is sheltered at Yajibei's house; Yajibei and Ushi have taken responsibility for her immediate safety.

chapters.title: Slaughter by the Riverside
chapters.end_summary: Kojirō returns downstream with Yajibei's party; surviving Obata students carry the conflict back to their school.

chapters.title: Shavings
chapters.end_summary: Akemi has fled Sumiya into the night; Kojirō is associated with Yajibei's group as its sword instructor.

chapters.title: The Owl
chapters.end_summary: Shinzō has left on a revenge mission; Kagenori is gravely ill at the depleted Obata School; Kojirō remains in Edo.

chapters.title: A Plate of Loaches
chapters.end_summary: Musashi and Sannosuke remain together at Hōtengahara after San'emon's burial; the boy's older sister is absent and her location unknown.

chapters.title: Like Teacher, Like Pupil
chapters.end_summary: Musashi and Iori live and work at the Hōtengahara cabin; their teacher-pupil bond and joint agricultural project are established.

chapters.title: Mountain Devils
chapters.end_summary: The village has repelled the brigands under Musashi's leadership; Sado returns toward his duties intending a later meeting.

chapters.title: First Planting
chapters.end_summary: Sado returns to Edo without Musashi; the cultivated fields continue under village solidarity; Musashi and Iori's destination is not disclosed here.

chapters.title: The Flies
chapters.end_summary: Musashi remains in Bakurōchō; Iori has departed alone with the letter and directions to Kobikichō.

chapters.title: The Soul Polisher
chapters.end_summary: Musashi returns to the inn and waits uneasily because Iori has not returned; he plans to move into Kōsuke's house.

chapters.title: The Fox
chapters.end_summary: Otsū and Hyōgo are near the Yagyū residence; Iori remains disoriented nearby and has not recognized Otsū.

chapters.title: An Urgent Letter
chapters.end_summary: Hyōgo and Otsū travel toward Koyagyū; Iori runs toward the Yagyū residence still carrying Musashi's letter.

chapters.title: Filial Piety
chapters.end_summary: Kojirō is at Yajibei's house; Osugi's return is supplied by the immediately following chapter's council, not assumed from this chapter alone.

chapters.title: Spring Shower in Red
chapters.end_summary: Jūrō and Koroku are dead; Shinzō is critically wounded in Kōsuke's arms; Kojirō has fled into the dark; Osugi survives the ditch fall.

chapters.title: A Block of Wood
chapters.end_summary: Musashi is heading to the Obata School; Iori stays at Kōsuke's; Shinzō is alive and recovering under care.

chapters.title: The Deserted Prophet
chapters.end_summary: Kagenori remains gravely ill; Yogorō has made a decision that the chapter does not reveal; Musashi's next location is unspecified.

chapters.title: The Talk of the Town
chapters.end_summary: Shinzō reaches the vicinity of his father's Ushigome home; Musashi departs alone; Iori remains in Kōsuke's household; the smear campaign is active across Edo.

events.description: Musashi walks ahead while Otsū rides the cow and Jōtarō accompanies her toward Fukushima.
Karasumaru’s letter allows Otsū and Jōtarō through the Fukushima checkpoint; Musashi has already gone ahead.
Matahachi attacks Jōtarō, takes the cow rope and carries Otsū away against her will.
Noticing the delay, Musashi runs back along the road to search.
Musashi follows reports and finds the abandoned cow associated with Gonnosuke's farmhouse.
A false accusation leads to a staff contest; Musashi pins Gonnosuke and his mother intervenes with a lance.
They establish that Gonnosuke found, rather than stole, the cow and reconcile.
A farmer's household reports Jōtarō ran toward Yabuhara and was directed to Daizō in Narai; Musashi and Gonnosuke cross the pond while continuing the search.
events.destination_label: the opposite side of Nobu Pond

events.description: Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Matahachi binds Otsū in the tiny shrine and renews his coercion, biting her arm.
A distant torch on the pond is seen, but no contact or identification on the spot occurs.
Matahachi seizes a farmer and horse; Otsū later secures the farmer's release.
They continue by the back route through Ina toward Kōshū and Edo.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi overhears the mother's demand for a rematch and slips away.
At Daizō's business Musashi learns that Daizō and Jōtarō have already departed, but their branch beyond Shiojiri is uncertain.
Gonnosuke catches Musashi and they conduct a formal second contest near the larches.
After mutual recognition, Musashi proceeds toward Kamisuwa while Gonnosuke and his mother separate from him.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi stops at the hot springs on Lake Suwa to bathe and tend his injury.
Ishimoda Geki identifies Musashi and hosts him overnight at the daimyō inn.
Geki urges Musashi to consider service under Date Masamune and discusses governance and the warrior's role.
Musashi does not accept the offer and continues considering his Way.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Geki leaves toward Wada Pass while Musashi resumes the search.
One hired laborer honestly reports that Daizō and Jōtarō went toward Wada.
At a roadside teahouse Musashi discovers Geki's money and letter hidden in his bag.
Bandits lure Musashi onto a ravine log; he kills the first attacker and comes under gunfire from the opposite bank.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi defeats the gunmen, wounds their leader and recognizes Gion Tōji.
Musashi recognizes Okō; the three exchange information about Akemi's reported movements.
Tōji and Okō trigger a collapsing guest-room trap, but Musashi escapes the fall.
Musashi ties Okō to a tree, burns the cabin and disappears before the band can find him.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Kojirō meets Jinnai's moving troupe at Kobotoke and continues toward Edo; Akemi hides briefly and rejoins.
Daizō, Sukeichi and Jōtarō visit Yakuōin and then proceed to Hachiōji.
Jōtarō recognizes Akemi; they exchange news and Akemi reacts with jealousy and distress.
After Akemi's moat-side crisis, the scarred rōnin knocks Jōtarō unconscious and sexually assaults Akemi; the chapter presents the assault through explicit aftermath and implication.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Jinnai's troupe, with Akemi restored to it, leaves Hachiōji before sunrise.
Jōtarō follows Daizō and witnesses him bury a large quantity of gold beneath a pine by the mound.
Daizō discovers the spying, binds Jōtarō to secrecy and declares that he is taking the boy under his protection.
Daizō, Sukeichi and Jōtarō continue toward Edo.
After two months of travel Osugi enters rapidly expanding Edo by the Takanawa route.
Osugi walks through the construction zones and reaches Nihombashi.
Yajibei catches a thief who attacked Osugi, recovers her property and orders Ushi to help her.
The injured Osugi is carried to Yajibei's Bakurōchō house.
The narrative establishes that Osugi has remained with Yajibei for roughly a year and a half.
Yajibei's party travels by boat to Sensōji; a donation plaque mentions Daizō but does not place him there.
Kojirō kills or disables the Obata swordsmen who confront him beside the river.
Kojirō meets Osugi and Yajibei and accepts an invitation onto their return boat.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Yajibei hires Kojirō to train his men three times a month.
Kojirō's first training session maims men and kills one trainee.
Kojirō, Jūrō and Koroku visit Sumiya and ask for Hanagiri.
Akemi, now called Hanagiri, avoids Kojirō and escapes into the darkness along the moat.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Ten Obata students ambush Kojirō on the road beside the new Edo moat; five are killed before the later school confrontation.
Shinzō tends Kagenori and condemns the students' unauthorized revenge.
Kojirō follows survivors home and openly humiliates the Obata group in the shrine grove.
Before Yogorō's expected return, Shinzō leaves a farewell letter and departs to kill Kojirō.
The chapter reports that Musashi briefly passed through Edo, traveled to Sendai to return Geki's money, then came back south to Shimōsa.
Musashi meets twelve-year-old Sannosuke catching loaches and follows him to the isolated shack.
Musashi helps the boy carry and bury his father San'emon, who died that morning.
After testing the orphan's resolve, Musashi accepts Sannosuke as his pupil.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi renames Sannosuke Iori, burns the old shack and builds a new cabin on a knoll.
They clear land and repeatedly attempt to create fields in the flood-prone plain.
During a storm Iori reaches Tokuganji and returns with supplies; the trip is explicitly narrated through his return account.
Musashi changes the water-and-field strategy; after winter and thaw the cultivation becomes stable enough to continue.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Sado stays at Tokuganji for his father's memorial anniversary and briefly meets Iori, who is collecting millet.
Iori witnesses the brigand raid, is tied to a bridge post, escapes and runs back to Musashi.
Musashi frees captives, organizes villagers into ambush groups and leads them against the raiders.
Sado investigates the next day, learns Musashi's name and sees his written injunction, but leaves without meeting him.
The narrative marks roughly a year and a half since Sado's Tokuganji visit.
Kakubei recommends his household guest Kojirō for Hosokawa service.
Tadatoshi agrees to inspect Kojirō and instructs Sado to locate the Musashi he previously praised.
At Hōtengahara Sado learns that Musashi and Iori vanished the morning after the first-planting celebration a month earlier.
Musashi and Iori pass the eastern barrier after Musashi names Yagyū Munenori as his Edo connection.
After the ferry crossing, Iori's pouch dispute reveals Jūrō as a Hangawara man; Jūrō recognizes Musashi's name.
Musashi uses the incident to teach Iori that etiquette restrains people's bad side and is essential in crowded civic life.
At the horse market Sukekurō recognizes Musashi and invites him to the Yagyū household, alluding to an unidentified 'beautiful treasure.'
When horse trader Kumagorō threatens him over noise complaints, Musashi silently plucks live flies from his soba with chopsticks, causing the traders to retreat.
Musashi replies that he will visit only for a bout and sends Iori with the letter toward the Yagyū residence.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Kōsuke initially refuses to polish Musashi's sword because he believes the owner seeks only a better killing edge.
Kōsuke explains Kōetsu's teaching that the craftsman's real work is polishing the samurai's soul and that a sword exists to preserve integrity and order, not delight in killing.
Musashi accepts the criticism and recognizes that he has not adequately considered the moral spirit of the sword he carries.
Their shared connection to Hon'ami Kōetsu changes the exchange; Kōsuke agrees to polish the blade.
Kōsuke offers an ancient sword in exchange for a Kannon carving and invites Musashi to lodge in his house.
Musashi recognizes Kojirō's Drying Pole among Kōsuke's commissions; the owner is not physically present.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Iori reaches the Yagyū storehouses, sleeps there and receives a rough map to the residence at Higakubo.
Iori loses time watching the castle and Hibiya construction before climbing toward Azabu.
After wounding a fox, Iori sees Otsū and Hyōgo but mistakes both for fox transformations and hides.
The narrative reports that Sukekurō rescued Otsū from Matahachi the previous year and brought her into Yagyū protection.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
A fast courier's letter from Shōda reports Sekishūsai's critical illness.
Munenori sends Hyōgo in his stead; Otsū obtains permission to accompany him and they depart that night.
Hyōgo and Otsū find the exhausted Iori, calm his fox panic and learn of his letter.
They direct Iori to the nearby Yagyū house, then resume their fast journey toward Sangen'ya and the Tōkaidō route.
events.destination_label: Sangen'ya and the Tōkaidō toward Koyagyū

events.description: Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Jūrō tells Osugi he saw Musashi at the Sumida ferry and had his lodging watched.
Impatient with delay, Osugi sets out alone for Kakubei's house on Isarago Hill to find Kojirō.
Jūrō sends Koroku after Osugi to see her safely to or back from Kakubei's house.
Kojirō enters while Jūrō and the men are emotionally affected by Osugi's copied filial-piety sutra.
Jūrō and the Hangawara men initially mock Osugi's sutra but become emotionally overwhelmed by its description of parental sacrifice and filial neglect.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
The four agree that Kojirō will lure Musashi out so Osugi can strike him the following night.
They take positions around Kōsuke's house while Kojirō goes to the door for his sword and asks for Musashi.
Shinzō, who had followed the party, kills Jūrō and Koroku and shoves Osugi into a ditch.
Kojirō cuts a severe wound from Shinzō's neck and flees as Kōsuke arrives to support the wounded man.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Kōsuke brings Shinzō home; the wound is cauterized and Musashi attributes its form to Kojirō's swallow-flight stroke.
After almost forty-eight hours of work, Musashi reduces the old block without producing the intended Kannon and stops to meditate.
Iori returns after three days, apologizes and gives Musashi Sukekurō's reply.
The reply postpones a Yagyū test; Musashi leaves to notify the Obata School while Iori remains to reflect on his conduct.
Iori blames his long delay on a fox; Musashi reframes the punishment as Iori's own invisible conscience reacting to his choices.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Musashi reports Shinzō's condition and warns Yogorō not to continue the feud with Kojirō.
After glimpsing Musashi from afar, Kagenori recognizes unusual alertness and orders Yogorō to bring him back.
Kagenori tells Yogorō that his military science is now aimed at peace and stability and that he needs the right mature man to receive it because Yogorō is not ready.
Yogorō searches the shrine grounds and Kōjimachi street but cannot find Musashi.
events.destination_label: Kōjimachi street and nearby shrine grounds

events.description: Handayū says the Hosokawa house already knows of Shinzō's defeat; Yogorō returns with an undisclosed decision.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
Recovering Shinzō decides to leave; Musashi insists on escorting him toward his father's Ushigome house.
Hangawara men surround the pair and demand Shinzō; Musashi argues against the vendetta and holds them off.
Musashi throws Tazaemon into the moat, carries Shinzō clear and then runs with him rather than fight the gang.
Musashi brings Shinzō within sight of his father's house near Akagi Myōjin and leaves without entering.
Hangawara propaganda spreads through Edo, publicly branding Musashi a coward and demanding he answer Osugi's revenge claim.
Additional chapter-scoped memories, reports or biographical references; no physical presence is asserted.
